title: adaptive-request-prioritization-and-fairness-onboarding-playbook-2026
author: Priya Raman
body:
TITLE: Adaptive Request Prioritization and Fairness — Enterprise Onboarding Playbook

SUMMARY
This playbook describes the recommended configuration, validation, and operational handoff for enabling tenant-aware request prioritization and fairness controls during enterprise onboarding. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and Platform SREs working with Dedicated or Private tenants who require predictable latency and cost isolation while preserving fair access across internal user groups.

AUDIENCE
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs)
- Platform SRE / Infra Onboarding Engineers
- Tenant Engineering Leads

SCOPE
This document covers:
1) Functional goals and acceptance SLOs for prioritization and fairness.
2) Configuration templates for ingress priority maps and quota-snooze windows.
3) Onboarding validation tests and telemetry queries.
4) Runbook for common failure modes and escalation flow.
5) Handoff checklist and post-go-live QBR signals.

OUT-OF-SCOPE
- Low-level kernel tuning for GPU runtime (see eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling).
- Billing reconciliation and invoicing (see finance-and-legal/procurement).

GOALS & ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile tail latency for gold-tier requests <= 180 ms under steady-state load (customer-defined).
- Isolation: Background batch/ingest traffic must not cause >10% degradation on gold-tier p95 latency.
- Fairness: No single API key or tenant-owner group should exceed 40% of overall capacity for more than 10 minutes without being auto-rate-limited or flagged.
- Observability: Dashboards and alerting must be present and validated before handoff.

KEY CONCEPTS
- Priority buckets: gold | silver | bronze — map to service-level CPU/GPU lanes and admission controls.
- Fairness window: sliding 5–15 minute window used to compute dominant share and trigger automated throttles.
- Snooze policy: temporary, scheduled relaxation of limits to allow business-critical bursts (e.g., monthly reports) with explicit expiry.

ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES
- Customer Success (owner): validate business intent, drive acceptance, coordinate stakeholders.
- Solutions Engineering (owner): produce tenant configuration, run pre-go-live simulations, produce the validation report.
- Platform SRE (owner): apply ingress policies, verify router behavior, enable telemetry & alerting.
- Customer Engineering (owner): provide representative workload, participate in game-day.

CONFIGURATION REFERENCE (EXAMPLE)
1) Ingress priority map (YAML):

--- yaml
# tenant-priority-map.yaml
tenant_id: tenant-acme-123
priority_map:
  - matcher: "/v1/generate*"
    default: gold
    overrides:
      - api_key_prefix: "acme-analytics-"
        priority: silver
      - route_header: "X-Batch-Job: true"
        priority: bronze
fairness_policy:
  enabled: true
  window_minutes: 10
  max_share_percent: 40
snooze_windows:
  - name: "monthly-reporting"
    start: "2026-06-15T02:00:00Z"
    duration_minutes: 90
    allowed_priorities: [gold, silver]
---

2) Admission control snippet (JSON) for router plugin:

{
  "plugin": "adaptive-admission",
  "config": {
    "base_concurrency": 8,
    "burst_tokens": 16,
    "fairshare_window_sec": 600,
    "dominant_share_threshold_pct": 40
  }
}

VALIDATION & TESTING CHECKLIST (pre-go-live)
1) Synthetic workload replay:
   - Run 30-minute mixed workload (60% chat, 30% embeddings, 10% batch) at 120% of expected baseline traffic.
   - Verify gold p95 <= configured SLO and bronze traffic is degraded gracefully.
2) Dominant-share stress test:
   - Simulate a single API key consuming 60% of capacity for 20 minutes — confirm automated throttle triggers at 40% threshold and alert fires.
3) Snooze test:
   - Apply snooze window for 90 minutes and verify elevated concurrency is allowed during the window and removed after expiry.
4) Failure injection:
   - Cause an ingress service restart and confirm fairshare bookkeeping recovers within 2 windows.

TELEMETRY & DASHBOARDS
Minimum telemetry required before handoff:
- Metrics (Prometheus naming conventions):
  - ingress_requests_total{tenant,priority,route}
  - ingress_latency_seconds_bucket{tenant,priority}
  - admission_rejected_total{tenant,reason}
  - dominant_share_percent{tenant}
- Alerts (examples):
  - alert: GoldP95LatencyBreach
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ingress_latency_seconds_bucket{priority="gold"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.18
    for: 5m
  - alert: DominantShareExceeded
    expr: max_over_time(dominant_share_percent[10m]) > 40
    for: 2m
- Dashboard panels to include:
  - Tenant capacity map (by priority lanes)
  - Dominant share trend and top-10 API keys
  - Admission rejects and reasons by route

GAME-DAY AND PRE-GO-LIVE RUN
1) Schedule a 90-minute game day with the customer and internal SRE/SEs.
2) Run the synthetic scenario; customer verifies UX and latency targets.
3) Exercise escalation flow (send a simulated dominant-share alert, perform manual throttle and policy rollback).
4) Capture runbook actions and update the confluence page with any deviations.

COMMON FAILURE MODES & RUNBOOK ACTIONS
1) Symptom: Gold p95 spikes but total ingress QPS is normal.
   - Probable cause: priority lane starvation due to misrouted bronze traffic.
   - Steps:
     1. Check ingress_requests_total by priority.
     2. If bronze >> expected, temporarily set bronze concurrency to 1 and watch gold p95.
     3. If resolved, roll back and apply more specific route matchers.
2) Symptom: Dominant-share throttle not triggering on heavy single-key usage.
   - Probable cause: Fairshare bookkeeping lag or misconfigured window.
   - Steps:
     1. Inspect dominant_share_percent metric for the API key.
     2. Confirm fairshare_window_sec in plugin config.
     3. If lagging, restart the bookkeeping worker with the trace flag enabled; engage eng-serving-runtime on-call if persistent.
3) Symptom: Snooze window did not expire.
   - Steps:
     1. Verify the scheduled task processed the expiry event (check /var/log/snooze-service).
     2. If the task failed, manually remove snooze and notify customer of corrective action.

ESCALATION PATHS
- Tier 1 (CSM/SE): initial troubleshooting and customer comms.
- Tier 2 (Platform SRE): policy verification, telemetry deep-dive, temporary policy changes.
- Tier 3 (Runtime Eng): kernel/runtime intervention, fairshare bookkeeping bugs, urgent fixes.
Escalation contacts (on-call rotation):
- Platform SRE on-call: pages -> #sre-oncall -> 10 min response target.
- Runtime Eng on-call: pages -> #runtime-oncall -> 15 min response target.

HANDOFF & DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
Before final handoff to Customer Success (long-term support):
- Completed validation report (attach synthetic run logs).
- Dashboard URL and playbook link.
- Confirmed alert routing to customer and Redwood Slack channel.
- Signed acceptance: CSM, SE, and Tenant Engineering Lead.

POST-GO-LIVE QBR SIGNALS (30/90/180 day)
- Usage concentration: fraction of traffic coming from top-3 API keys — target < 60%.
- SLO breaches per month for priority lanes.
- Number of manual snooze windows and business justification.
- Cost delta attributed to prioritization changes (included in QBR template).

CHANGE CONTROL & ROLL-BACK
- All changes to priority maps or admission control config must go through the change management process (policies-and-process/change-management).
- Rollback procedure: revert to previous config via the platform config-store with a tagged release and monitor metrics for 20 minutes.

APPENDIX A — SAMPLE PROMQL QUERIES
- Gold p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ingress_latency_seconds_bucket{tenant="tenant-acme-123",priority="gold"}[5m])) by (le))
- Dominant share for API key k: max_over_time( dominant_share_percent{tenant="tenant-acme-123",api_key="k"}[10m])
